analysis:
Both units are head-side text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 4678-5521). The patch excerpt shows only documentation edits (a stop-request paragraph near line 453 and some GLM/cluster sections). No source code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation or authorization logic changes in this PR, so there is no executable behavior to regress.

I checked the documented security-relevant statements against the threat model and found no contradiction:
- Flint tool/response-format constraints (4688-4796): fail-closed validation, with a 400 or 422 on malformed output. This does not conflict with T-008, T-010 or T-027.
- The Flint context bound is enforced before SSE headers (4798-4803), which is availability-positive.
- Cluster listeners, pairing and unpairing docs (4966-5210): the link handshake is keyed to the pairing edge secret and the pairing identity compares pins and epoch. The docs describe the existing control lease and the Pair again / Start over flows and add no new trust boundary. The stopsAsked counter is a doc-described setup-record field. I could not verify its authentication, because the code is not in the supplied evidence. It is a cluster-control matter outside the listed TBs and outside this docs-only diff.
- Link and share probe history files are described as owner-only (5294, 5406). That is consistent with the local-file posture. They hold only timing and hardware metadata, not prompt data (A-001), and are not prefix-cache artifacts, so T-041 is unaffected.
- The GLM paired-control retirement text (5246-5263) describes existing fail-closed behavior.

The patch excerpt is truncated, so the full diff of the changed ranges at base 453 and 3219 and head 453-473, 3239 and 3255-3286 was only partly visible. The doc statements about cluster-control stop counting were not checked against code, but that is a documentation-only concern. No threat-model update is needed from this doc-only change.
